meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wait, to expect', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрыть'.

'закрывать глаза на' + accusative. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрыть'.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.note: Of a person: я занят = I'm busy. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied
Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'отвечать'.
Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ветить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to answer, to reply', paired with 'отвечать'.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'этому').

examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'порить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to argue, to dispute', paired with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
